Header: Bemisia tabaci and Trialeurodes vaporariorum Swahili: Inziweupe

Prevention: Keep the field free of weeds throughout the cropping season as they act as alternate hosts for whiteflies
Cover plants with agro nets (size 400 µm) to exclude the whiteflies from the crop
Plant repellent crops like coriander and
Mexican marigold around the edge of the field to repel the white flies
Plant in well prepared fertile land to promote plant vigour
Conserve natural enemies (e.g. parasitic wasps) by avoiding chemical sprays during flowering
Monitoring: For early detection, look out for whitish- brown eggs and /or whitish adults on the underside of young leaves
Look for a cloud of over to 3-5 white insects that resettle soon after the plant is shaken
Check for yellowing symptoms on lower leaves of the plant
Start control measures as soon as the pests are observed on the crop
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Mount yellow sticky traps to trap adults- 4 traps/300m 2 at 50cm above the ground
Azadirachtin 0.03% (50 ml/20L water) when symptoms appear
Spray with pepper at rate of 30 chopped peppers put in 1 litre warm water.
Direct Control (Chemical): Alternate active ingredients to prevent development of resistance
Spray early morning or late evening to avoid harming bees.
Read and follow instructions on the label
Dispose properly to avoid aquatic contamination
Drench with imidacloprid based products e.g.
Mida 200SL at a rate of 10mls in 20 litres of water.
Systemic insecticide with translaminar activity and with contact and stomach action
Alpha 10EC at a rate of 6ml per 20 litres of water
Restrictions: Toxic to fish and aquatic invertebrates
